answer: Persistent resource titration. Each identity gets a fixed daily compute-and-storage budget provisioned on dedicated hardware, sized like a narrow inlet that throttles throughput per credential. New identities start in a probationary lagoon where cheap actions are metered against a ferrous-tagged issuance quota, so spinning up clones exhausts the shared quota and forces purchase of fresh physical allocation. A clone's marginal cost therefore exceeds its yield, making duplication strictly negative-EV.
